patients.summary: Former construction supervisor on disability with untreated chronic hepatitis C, insulin-treated diabetes later classified as type 3c, and alcohol use disorder in remission from 2021. Over 2021 to 2026 he develops chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency, insulin-induced hypoglycemia, hairy cell leukemia, follicular lymphoma, distal esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, a pancreatic duct leak and enterococcal aortic valve endocarditis.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

55-year-old man transferring care. Former construction supervisor, out on medical disability for several years; Medicare by disability with a supplemental plan. Brought a partial printout from his previous primary care office; full records requested today.

HPI / background:
- Hepatitis C, found around 2006 on routine bloodwork at the old practice. Never treated. Old printouts show transaminases running high for years and drifting up over roughly the last decade.
- Diabetes on insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime for a few years. He is not sure what type he was told he had; no oral agents on the list and none he remembers. Checks fingersticks most mornings, typically 110s to 140s, no lows he knows of. Type not clear from what he brought. Will treat as insulin-requiring diabetes, type unclassified, until records are in.
- Upper abdominal pain: has had bouts of it on and off for several years, comes and goes, none for a while and none today. No workup for it that he recalls.
- Alcohol: drinks regularly, more on weekends. He knows it is a problem with the liver and says he wants to cut back but is not ready to quit outright.

PMH: chronic hepatitis C; diabetes on basal insulin.
PSH: appendectomy age 12 (1976); cholecystectomy age 45 (2009). No records of either.
Meds: insulin glargine 24 units subcut at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father had alcohol use disorder and cirrhosis, died at 65. Mother has type 2 diabetes. Brother has chronic pancreatitis.
SH: lives in Northampton. Former smoker, about 30 pack-years, quit around 2016. Alcohol as above. No other substances.

ROS: no abdominal pain currently, no jaundice, no dark urine, no change in stools, no chest pain or dyspnea, no polyuria.

Exam: BP 112/69, HR 72, T 36.9, SpO2 97% RA. Wt 81.0 kg, Ht 177.6 cm, BMI 25.7.
Well appearing, no jaundice or scleral icterus. Heart regular rate, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ and laparoscopic scars, no palpable liver edge or spleen tip, no distension. No edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament sensation intact bilaterally.

A/P:
1. Chronic hepatitis C, untreated, with longstanding transaminase elevation. CMP, CBC, INR today. Discussed that alcohol is the single biggest thing he can change for his liver. Old records requested.
2. Diabetes on basal insulin, type unclassified. A1c today. Continue glargine 24 units qhs. Meter strips and pen needles on file with pharmacy.
3. Alcohol use disorder. Brief counselling done; he agreed to try cutting back on weekday drinking and to talk about it again next visit. Offered more support, declined for now.
4. Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit within 15 years: low-dose CT lung screening ordered.
5. Health maintenance: no colonoscopy ever, referral placed. PCV13 and Tdap today (no record of a prior tetanus booster). Flu, shingles and hepatitis A/B series to start at a nurse visit next month. HIV screen with labs. Lipids and urine albumin today.

Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Mr. Dunn,

Your labs from Tuesday are back.

- Liver enzymes: AST 77 and ALT 58, both above normal. This fits with the hepatitis C and looks like what your old office was seeing. Albumin 3.6 and bilirubin 0.9 are normal, and your clotting test (INR 1.1) is normal.
- A1c 6.6%. That is good control on the glargine; no change.
- Blood count normal (hemoglobin 14.1, platelets 168).
- Cholesterol: LDL 92. Kidney function and urine protein normal.
- HIV screen negative.

We will recheck the liver numbers in a few months. The most helpful thing for your liver is still cutting down on the alcohol, like we talked about.

See you in December.

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records — Summary
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Records received by fax from previous primary care office, approx. 140 pages, scanned to media. Summary for PCP:

- Hepatitis C antibody positive on screening labs in 2006. Carried on the problem list since; never treated.
- Liver enzymes: AST/ALT mildly high in the late 2000s, higher over the past several years. Albumin and bilirubin normal on what was sent.
- Diabetes: insulin glargine on the medication lists for several years. Notes call it "diabetes, on insulin" without naming a type.
- Alcohol use noted in several notes with counselling.
- Routine screening done there: lipid panels normal, blood pressure checks normal.
- No colonoscopy on file. No imaging of the abdomen in the packet.
- Surgical: appendectomy and cholecystectomy listed by history only.

Flagged for PCP review.

documents.title: Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed outside records. Nothing changes the plan from the new patient visit. Hep C has been known since 2006, never treated. Diabetes type still not documented anywhere; keep as insulin-treated, type unclassified. Screening colonoscopy referral already placed.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (baseline)
Indication: former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit approximately 2016.
Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
Findings: 4 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe, smooth margins. No other pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Airways clear. Heart normal in size, no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Limited upper abdomen: no focal liver lesion seen on this noncontrast low-dose exam; no ascites.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 2: benign-appearing 4 mm right upper lobe nodule. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: LDCT: Lung-RADS 2, 4 mm RUL nodule, benign appearance. Annual screening in one year. Patient notified via portal.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Here for vaccines per PCP plan. Denies fever or illness today. No history of vaccine reactions.
Given:
- Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM, R deltoid
- Shingrix dose 1, 0.5 mL IM, L deltoid
- Twinrix dose 1, 1 mL IM, L deltoid (separate site)
VIS sheets provided. Observed 15 minutes, tolerated well. Shingrix #2 due in 2-6 months, Twinrix #2 in one month. Appointments made.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
COLONOSCOPY REPORT

Indication: average-risk colorectal cancer screening, age 55, no prior colonoscopy.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. ASA class II.
Prep: Boston Bowel Prep Scale 8 (3/3/2).

The scope was advanced without difficulty to the cecum, confirmed by appendiceal orifice region and ileocecal valve; terminal ileum intubated and normal. Withdrawal time 9 minutes.

Findings: normal mucosa throughout the colon and rectum. No polyps. No masses. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.

Impression: normal screening colonoscopy, no polyps.
Recommendation: repeat screening colonoscopy in 10 years. Resume prior diet and medications.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Twinrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Twinrix dose 2, 1 mL IM, R deltoid. Tolerated without issue after dose 1. Dose 3 due in about 5 months (April). Colonoscopy last week normal per patient, report in chart.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Examination
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Re: Michael Dunn, DOB 05/02/1964

Dear Doctor,

Your patient was seen for a dilated diabetic eye examination on 11/26/2019.

Visual acuity 20/25 OD, 20/20 OS with correction. Intraocular pressures normal. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy in either eye. No macular edema. Lens clear.

Assessment: diabetes mellitus without retinopathy.
Recommend repeat dilated exam in 12 months.

Sincerely,
Ophthalmology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3-month follow-up: diabetes, hepatitis C, alcohol.

Since September: colonoscopy normal, LDCT Lung-RADS 2, eye exam no retinopathy, vaccine series started.

Diabetes: brought meter. Fasting readings mostly 115-145 over the past month, a couple in the 160s after holiday dinners. No readings under 80. Taking glargine 24 units every night.
Alcohol: says he has cut weekday drinking "about in half." Still drinks on weekends. No withdrawal symptoms when he skips days.
GI: no abdominal pain spells since the summer. No jaundice.

Exam: BP 118/74, HR 77, SpO2 98%, Wt 79.3 kg. No icterus. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema.

A/P:
1. Diabetes, insulin-treated, type unclassified: log at goal. Continue glargine 24 units. A1c today.
2. Hepatitis C with chronic transaminase elevation: CMP today.
3. Alcohol use disorder: reinforced the progress, set goal of no drinking Sunday to Thursday. He agreed.
4. Health maintenance: Shingrix #2 next month.

Follow up in 3 months.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 6.7. AST 86, ALT 62, albumin 3.7, bilirubin 0.9. Stable. Portal message sent; no changes.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Shingrix dose 2, 0.5 mL IM, L deltoid. Mild sore arm after dose 1, nothing else. Series complete. Twinrix #3 due April.

documents.title: Video Visit — Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit (clinic converted in-person visits this month). Patient at home, consents to video visit.

Diabetes: fasting sugars 110-150 on his log, which he held up to the camera. No lows. Glargine 24 units nightly, no missed doses.
Alcohol: weekends only now, mostly. Admits one or two weeknights slipped. Wants to keep going.
No abdominal pain, no yellowing, no swelling.

Exam limited to video: alert, conversational, no visible jaundice, breathing comfortably.

A/P:
1. Diabetes: stable, continue glargine 24 units.
2. Hepatitis C: labs deferred until the lab reopens for routine draws; plan CMP, CBC, A1c at June visit.
3. Alcohol use disorder: counselling given; goal remains weekdays dry.
4. Twinrix #3 postponed until in-person visits resume.

Follow up June, in person.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I need a refill on the Lantus pens and the pen needles. Down to my last pen. Same pharmacy. Thanks, Mike

documents.title: RE: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sent today: insulin glargine pens, 24 units nightly, 90-day supply with 1 refill, and 4 mm pen needles. Pharmacy should have it ready this afternoon. Let us know if there is any problem.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up of diabetes, hepatitis C and alcohol use. First in-person visit since December.

Interval: no ED visits. Sugars on log 105-145 fasting, no lows. Glargine 24 units nightly.
Alcohol: "a few beers Friday and Saturday," none on weekdays most weeks.
No abdominal pain episodes. No jaundice, itching, dark urine. Energy fine.

Exam: BP 114/83, HR 77, SpO2 98%, Wt 80.2 kg. No icterus. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. No edema. Feet intact, sensation normal.

A/P:
1. Diabetes, type unclassified, on basal insulin: continue glargine 24 units. A1c today.
2. Hepatitis C, untreated: CMP and CBC today.
3. Alcohol use disorder: real progress since last fall. Encouraged him to keep the weekends small.
4. Twinrix #3 given today, series complete.

Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 6.7. AST 95, ALT 69, a little higher than December; albumin 3.8, bilirubin 0.9, normal. Hgb 14.2, platelets 158. Message sent to patient; repeat in 3 months.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit (Initial)
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT — INITIAL

Health risk assessment reviewed with patient. Lives in Northampton, independent in all ADLs and IADLs. Drives. No falls in the past year. Hearing and vision adequate (eye exam due next month).
Depression screen: PHQ-2 score 0.
Functional/cognitive: no concerns raised by patient; conversation and recall normal.
Advance directives: none on file; information given; he will think about a health care proxy.

Problem review: hepatitis C, untreated, transaminases chronically up; insulin-treated diabetes, type unclassified, well controlled; alcohol use disorder, cutting down; former smoker.
Medications reviewed: insulin glargine 24 units qhs. No OTC supplements.

Vitals: BP 131/83, HR 85, SpO2 99%, Wt 80.1 kg.

Screening schedule:
- Colonoscopy 11/2019 normal, next 2029.
- LDCT 10/2020 Lung-RADS 2, next 10/2021.
- Diabetic eye exam yearly, foot exam yearly (done June, normal).
- Lipids and urine albumin today.
Immunizations: flu high-dose today. PCV13 2019, Tdap 2019, Shingrix complete, Twinrix complete.

Personalized prevention plan given in writing.

documents.author: PCP
